ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a three-phase bridge inverter, the DC bus is labeled Vd, and the upper and lower bridge arms contain ideal switches S1, S3, S5 and S4, S6, S2. Inside the dashed box on the right side is a three-phase balanced load, drawn as a star-connected resistive load, in which each phase resistance is labeled R = 20 Ω, and the phase voltage Vph is marked. Reasoning: The problem gives Vd = 300 V, and uses the 180° conduction mode. For a three-phase 180° conduction inverter with a balanced star load and a floating neutral point, the phase voltage of a certain phase takes the values +2Vd/3, +Vd/3, −Vd/3, −2Vd/3 in one period, and is repeatedly distributed according to standard 60° intervals. Its mean square value is Vph,rms^2 = (2/9)Vd^2. Substituting Vd = 300 V gives Vph,rms^2 = (2/9) × 300^2 = 20000 V^2. The resistance of each phase is R = 20 Ω, so the total three-phase power P = 3Vph,rms^2/R = 3 × 20000 / 20 = 3000 W = 3.0 kW.

Calculate its RMS square: Vph,rms^2 = (2/9)Vd^2. Then total power is 3Vph,rms^2/R = 3(2/9)(300^2)/20 = 3000 W = 3.0 kW.
